public_rationale: During 2024, substantive copyright litigation continued against several image-generation developers, while major record labels filed separate cases against Suno and Udio. These records support the ordinary reading that litigation became a prominent, sustained issue across generative-AI sectors. They do not establish that 2024 had the most lawsuits of any year or that plaintiffs generally prevailed; neither requirement was stated.
limitations: The result depends on the ordinary qualitative reading of year of litigation.
The evidence is a set of significant U.S. proceedings, not a worldwide annual lawsuit census.
Complaints establish disputes, not the truth of their infringement allegations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: 2024 is on track to be the year of generative AI litigation.

statement.excerpt: If 2023 was the year of GenAI, 2024 is still on track to be the year of GenAI litigation.
statement.document_title: No, multimodal ChatGPT is not going to “trivially” solve Generative AI's copyright problems

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that generative-AI copyright litigation will be a prominent, sustained industry issue during 2024.
The phrase does not specify a lawsuit count or require 2024 to exceed every earlier or later year.
The introductory reference to 2023 is a rhetorical comparison, not an operative condition requiring separate proof.
The surrounding discussion establishes copyright as the relevant litigation category.
criteria.support_condition: Multiple significant copyright disputes across generative-AI developers and creative sectors are filed or substantively litigated during 2024, demonstrating sustained industry relevance.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The year's record shows only isolated, short-lived disputes and no sustained major copyright proceedings involving generative-AI developers.
